title: Quant-iT PicoGreen dsDNA Quantification
author: Roey Angel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b2etqben
materials: Take out all reagents from the fridge and bring them to room temperature. Take out the DNA samples from the freezer. DNA samples should be slowly thawed on ice. Quant-iT™PicoGreen ® dsDNA reagent is dissolved in dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO), which freezes below 19 °C. The reagent must be completely thawed before using it by bringing it to room temperature. After the reagent thawed, it is advisable to briefly vortex the tube to make sure it is adequately mixed and to spin it down in a centrifuge or a mini centrifuge. Quant-iT™PicoGreen ® dsDNA reagent is light sensitive and should be protected from light at all times. Quant-iT™ PicoGreen™ dsDNA Assay Kit Invitrogen - Thermo Fisher Catalog #P11496

steps.title: Prepare 1X TE Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 22 ml of 1X TE buffer in a sterile, nuclease-free 50 ml tube.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 1.1 ml of 20X TE buffer into 20.9 ml of nuclease-free water.
Mix by inverting the tube several times.

steps.title: Prepare DNA Standard Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the DNA-standard work solutions for high-range and low-range quantification.

substeps.instruction: For high-range: Dilute the DNA-standard stock solution (λ DNA 100 ng µl-1) to 2 ng µl-1 by mixing 10 µl stock solution with 490 µl 1X TE buffer.
For low-range: Prepare a 40-fold dilution of the 2 ng µl-1 work solution by mixing 5 μl of the 2 ng µl-1 solution with 195 μl 1X TE buffer to yield a 0.05 ng µl-1 solution.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Dilutions
steps.instruction: If necessary, dilute each sample in 1X TE buffer to ensure readings fall within the dynamic range. It is recommended to run samples in duplicates.

steps.title: Prepare PicoGreen Work Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the PicoGreen work solution in a sterile and nucleic-acids free 50 ml tube.

substeps.instruction: Mix 9950 µL 1X TE buffer with 50 µL PicoGreen®.
Mix and protect the solution from light.

steps.title: Set Up 96-Well Plate
steps.instruction: Prepare a black, sterile, 96-well microtiter plate (Nunc, 265301, black, flat bottom).

substeps.instruction: Prepare the standard mixture in the first two columns of the plate.
Pipette 99 µl of 1X TE buffer into the remaining wells.

steps.title: Add DNA Samples
steps.instruction: Add unknown DNA samples to the remaining wells of the plate.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 1 µl of the unknown DNA samples into the wells.
Use a diluted sample if the concentration is expected to be higher than the dynamic range limit, or a larger volume if expected to be below the detection limit.

steps.title: Add PicoGreen Work Solution
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µl of the PicoGreen work solution into each well, including both standard and unknown sample wells.

steps.title: Incubate Plate
steps.instruction: Protect the 96-well plate from light and incubate for 2-5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Measure Fluorescence
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a plate reader (e.g., BioTek Synergy 2) and measure fluorescence using the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Excitation: ~480 nm
Emission: ~520 nm
Integration time: 40 s
Lag time: 0 s
Gain: Optimal (or fixed value, e.g., 100)
Number of flashes: 10
Calculated well: highest standard
Shaking: 5 s

steps.title: Calculate DNA Concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the DNA concentrations of the unknown samples using linear regression.

substeps.instruction: Plot measured fluorescent values of standard samples against known concentrations and fit a linear curve (R2 should typically be > 0.99).
Calculate concentrations in unknown samples using the slope and intercept parameters of the linear equation.
Output values are in ng µl-1, assuming 1 µl of sample was used.
Account for any sample dilutions when calculating the final concentration.
